A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LoRAverse paper and complete supplementary material. All 17 pages, including figures, tables, equations, and supplementary Sections 7–17, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation evaluations, retrieval ablations, timing measurements, VLM assessments, and a user study with 51 participants, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–3 and the supplementary qualitative and user-study results.

M1.justification: Concept extraction, clustering, greedy submodular retrieval, safety checking, and adapter combination are unchanged. Section 4 and the supplementary implementation and prompt descriptions retain the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same StylusDocsv2 adapter database, MS-COCO and PartiPrompts evaluation coverage, user-study scenarios, and supplementary Flux-compatible adapter experiment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Stylus and SD v1.5 in the main comparisons, cosine-similarity retrieval in the ablation, and RTop-100, RTop-500, and Random in supplementary Table 3.

E3.justification: The checkpoints, 35 denoising steps, retrieval settings, evaluation metrics, and sample sizes match. Both retain the 15,000-image quantitative evaluation and the 120-image study with 51 participants.

E4.justification: The CFG analysis, retrieval ablation, relevance/diversity parameter analyses, timing analysis, and supplementary cluster/concept-count sensitivity study are retained without revised evidence.

E5.justification: Aggregate-score reporting and user-rating distributions are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains LoRAverse's CLIP score of 25.07, TCE of 22.63, and user preference of 47.55%; supplementary Table 3 is also unchanged.

T1.justification: The submodularity definition, objectives and derivations, and all three lemmas with their proofs in supplementary Section 8 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about submodular adapter retrieval improving diversity while maintaining prompt alignment. No scientific contribution is added or redefined.

C2.justification: The CLIP/diversity interpretation, computational-overhead discussion, and supplementary limitations concerning clustering errors and societal biases remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, generation settings, clustering hyperparameters, complete LLM prompts, timing information, and resource-access information are unchanged. No implementation or reproducibility details are added.

R1.justification: The same 44 references and related-work positioning are retained. The added ICCV 2025 publication note supplies publication metadata without changing the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds a first-page footnote stating publication in the ICCV 2025 proceedings and updates the arXiv version/date identifier. Scientific prose, section order, and supplementary organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional footnote reflows the abstract and introduction across pages 1–2. Embedded figure images are resampled, but all 14 figures and five tables retain their examples, data, captions, order, and structure.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the scientific content, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information throughout the paper and supplement. The publication note clarifies provenance, while reflow and image resampling leave the presented evidence and ordinary readability materially unchanged.
